sentences.text: The genus Therizinosaurus contains only one known species, Therizinosaurus cheloniformis.
This large therizinosaurid could grow up to 10 meters long, stand 5 meters high, and possibly weigh 5 tons.
It possessed a proportionally small skull with a horny beak situated atop a long neck.
The animal had large, well-developed arms, a robust pelvic girdle suited for sitting, and a robust, shortened hindlimb structure.
Each of its arms measured a total of 2.4 to 2.5 meters in length, featuring a single scythe-shaped claw.
The tibia of Therizinosaurus was stocky and robust, being widest at its lower end.
Therizinosaurus possessed the longest known manual claw bones of any land animal, exceeding 50 cm in length.
That length does not include the horny sheath that must have surrounded the claw, with which it could have reached a length of 1 meter.
Measurements in 2018 showed that the arm bones of Therizinosaurus were resilient enough to generate significant forces.
These dimensions make Therizinosaurus the largest known therizinosaurid and the largest known maniraptoran.
The genus Therizinosaurus was scientifically described by Evgeny Maleev in 1954.
The first fossils were discovered in 1948 by a Mongolian expedition in the Gobi Desert at the Nemegt locality, also known as Nemegt Valley.
Fossils of Therizinosaurus have been found in the Nemegt Formation of the Gobi Desert.
Therizinosaurus was likely a slow-moving, long-necked browser with a beak and wide torso used for processing food.
It possessed a large gut adapted for processing foliage.
Research suggests Therizinosaurus likely used its hands in a hook-and-pull motion to grasp vegetation rather than for digging.
Digital simulations by Lautenschlager indicated that the curved claws of Therizinosaurus were poorly suited for scratching or digging.
Therizinosaurus was one of the tallest dinosaurs in the Nemegt Formation due to its high-browsing lifestyle.
It was a very tall animal, likely having reduced competition for foliage in its habitat and surpassing predators like Tarbosaurus.
The elongated claws of Therizinosaurus may have been used for self-defense or to intimidate predators like Tarbosaurus.
Therizinosaurus likely had sparse feathering.
Therizinosaurus arms were resistant to stress, suggesting they were used for both foraging and self-defense.
Therizinosaurus is classified within the dinosaur clade Theropoda as a maniraptoran.
The genus was assigned to its own family, Therizinosauridae, because it differed significantly from other known taxa.
Therizinosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 69 to 66 million years ago.
It lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now Asia.
It is debated whether Therizinosaurus was a turtle-like reptile, a hypothesis proposed by its original describer Maleev.
Lindsay E. Zanno's 2010 reevaluation debated the classification of specimen MPC-D 100/45, ultimately considering its referral to Therizinosaurus likely.
Rozhdestvensky suggested in 1970 that the claws might have been used to open termite mounds or for a fruit-eating diet.
